title: Red spider mite on papaya - Kenya

Header: Red spider mite on papaya - Kenya

Prevention: Improve soil water holding capacity by applying mulch and organic manure at the rate of 1 debe (18kg) per hole.
Practice good field sanitation e.g. remove and burn infested crop residues immediately after harvest, keep fields weed free.
Establish nurseries away from infested crops and avoid planting next to infested fields.
Monitoring: Scout weekly to check for red spider mite infestations.
Look on the underside of affected leaves for mites (tiny moving specks that are red or yellow-greenish) and whitish particles (shed skins of mites).
Tap leaf on white paper to see the mites.
Monitor for clusters of yellow spots on leaves which appear chlorotic.
When a few yellow spots and a few spider mites (5-7) are seen on three leaves per plant consider direct control.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Remove and burn all infected plant parts.
Irrigate the crop regularly to reduce heavy mite infestation.
Use neem (azadirachtin) at 20-50ml in 20 litres of water 3-4 times per season.
Phytoseiulus persimilis (Phytotech packaging. 2000 mites/400mls carrier material, Application is 1 million mites/ha i.e. 500 botlles/ha or 100 dudus/ M 2 .
Direct Control (Chemical): When using pesticides, read and follow instructions on the label.
Alternate active ingredients to prevent development of resistance.
Spray early morning or late evening to avoid harming bees.
Dust with sulphur - don’t use sulfur if temperatures exceed 32 degrees
C, and don’t apply sulfur within 30 days of an oil spray.
Malathion at a rate of 40-50ml in 20 litres of water.
Non-systemic pesticide with contact, stomach and respiratory action.
EC at the rate of 40-60mls per 20lt, 2-3 lts/ha.
Non-systemic pesticide with contact, stomach action as well as a slight repellent effect.
Restrictions: Use a maximum of 3 sprays per season.
